name: Open the Strategy Room — The Lumen Atlas Planning Cycle
description: A four-round, advanced strategy simulation set inside the Lumen Atlas Foundation, a Cambridge (UK) non-profit that runs Atlas — one of the world's ten most-visited reference sites: 14 million volunteer-edited articles, 480 million monthly readers, GBP 92M of mostly small-donor revenue, 340 staff but 240,000 active volunteer editors who expect to be consulted on anything that touches the platform. On 4 March 2026 the Board orders a 2026–2031 strategy in 90 days (AI-content response, a new revenue line, a governance update) — and within 48 hours a volunteer leaks the memo to the community forum. Playing the Chief Strategy Officer, you must run the planning cycle in full public view, with a hard 15 June Board deadline (miss it and the Board appoints the external consultancy that triggered the 2021 revolt). The simulation operationalises Loizos Heracleous's study of open, dialogic strategy-making at Wikimedia: inclusion (who participates) and transparency (what is shared) are two independent, costed dials, not one open/closed switch. Round 1 — assign each of nine stakeholder groups (core editors, casual editors, chapter affiliates, major donors, small donors, staff, the Board, partner institutions, readers) an inclusion level (co-create / consult / inform / exclude) inside a GBP 600K, 10-week participation budget. Round 2 — set transparency per phase (problem framing, option generation, financial modelling, recommendation) and choose input channels, deciding when the GBP 20M AI-licensing figure becomes public. Round 3 — reconcile 740 proposals clustering into four irreconcilable camps (purist / license-to-AI / premium tier / status-quo) into a single coherent five-year spine of at most three priorities, choosing what to reject and how to tell rejected camps they were heard. Round 4 — win the split Board vote (three community-elected trustees, four appointed) WHILE holding community legitimacy, and respond to a live editing-freeze threat from 600 editors without surrendering coherence or capitulating by ultimatum. The math rewards costed inclusion, phase-dependent transparency, reconciliation-by-rejection, and winning approval and legitimacy together — and punishes the five classic errors: maximal co-creation that blows the budget and deadline, premature transparency on half-formed figures, averaging all four camps into a focus-free plan, winning the vote while losing the community-elected trustees, and instant capitulation to a loud faction. Final KPIs track Buy-in, Idea Quality, Legitimacy and Coherence.

4 March 2026 · Lumen Atlas Foundation, Cambridge UK · The memo has leaked — run the strategy in full public view

Open the Strategy Room

You are the Chief Strategy Officer of a 480-million-reader non-profit run by 240,000 volunteers. The Board wants a five-year plan in 90 days; the community already has the leaked memo. Decide who enters the room, how transparent to be, how to reconcile four warring camps — and win the 15 June vote without losing the people the plan depends on.

Round 1 — Map the Room

Your Decisions This Round

Assign an inclusion level to each of the nine stakeholder groups. Co-create is deep and dear; consult is structured input; inform is one-way; exclude is silence. You have £600K and 10 weeks — co-create everyone and you blow both.

Co-create ≈ £120K & 4 wks each · Consult ≈ £45K & 1.5 wks · Inform ≈ £8K & 0.3 wks · Exclude is free but carries a revolt risk for the wrong group.

Set how open each phase is. Full transparency maximises legitimacy but exposes half-formed options; closed modelling protects coherence but reads as the 2021 betrayal. Get the timing of the GBP 20M figure right.

Final recommendation

740 proposals cluster into four irreconcilable camps. You cannot adopt all four. Build one spine of at most three priorities — choose which camps you actually pick, decide the AI-licensing question, and close the loop with those you reject.

The split Board votes today: three community-elected trustees, four appointed. You must win approval AND hold legitimacy — they cannot be traded. And this morning, 600 editors threaten a 30-day editing freeze unless the AI-licensing clause is withdrawn.

Facilitator (the Board chair & the community forum)
Two clocks are running: the 15 June Board deadline and the patience of 240,000 volunteers who already have your memo. Openness is not free — every voice you invite costs budget, weeks, and coherence, and every voice you exclude costs legitimacy. Set inclusion and transparency as two separate dials, reconcile by choosing not by averaging, and remember that winning the vote against the community is still a loss.
